family: one growing block of 1s beside a slowly growing disordered region
summary: A block of 1s at the left end grows by about one cell per sweep (43,506 cells after 2·10^9 steps) while a disordered region of about 1,500 cells on its right, never repeating, does the work; open.
title: What is known about 1RB1RA_1LC1RE_---0LD_1LE1LD_0RA0LF_1LF0LB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RA_1LC1RE_---0LD_1LE1LD_0RA0LF_1LF0LB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Most of the tape is a single block of 1s that grows by about a cell per sweep; the behavior that matters happens in a slowly growing disordered region beside it, which is not understood.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (C0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 32,607 cells have been visited and 31,699 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.512). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: For every length n of the run and any tape around it: L A> 1^n R reaches L 1^n A> R; L 1^n D> 1 R reaches L D> 1 1^n R. These are the moves the head makes across the long uniform stretches of the tape.

claims.title: No halt in the first 2·10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: tools/c/tmrun.c runs 2·109 steps without a halt; the left end is visited 45,734 times, with a different disordered region each time.

claims.title: Counter-like changes next to the block
claims.text: Over the 17,520 visits of the left end up to 3·108 steps, comparing each region with the previous one from its far end: the changed part is next to the block, at least 20 cells long in 56% of the visits, 80 in 14%, 320 in 0.4%, 640 in 0.01%. The commonest changes are a few fixed rewrites of the cells next to the block (0101010100 → 010101011 with N+2, 3,337 times).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It halts exactly when state C reads a 0, which would have to happen in the disordered region.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Almost all of this machine's tape is one block of 1s, growing by about a cell each time the head sweeps across it; all the interesting work happens in a small, messy region next to it.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator.
Length of the big block at 2·10<sup>9</sup> steps; the messy region is about 1,500 cells.
Crossing the block of 1s both ways, proved for every length.

sections.heading: A long block and a messy engine
html: Each sweep the head comes out of the disordered region on the right, runs left through the block of 1s, turns at the end of the tape in state E and runs back. Lean proves both crossings for every length. The block gains about one cell per visit:

The disordered region, about 1,500 cells of short runs at 2·109 steps (0 1 0 1 0 1 0 1 0^2 1^2 0 1^4 0 1 0 1 …), grows slowly and never repeats: its contents differed at all 45,734 visits of the left end. So it is not a small finite controller; it carries its own unbounded structure, and the halt (state C reading a 0) would have to come from there.

sections.heading: The region works like the low end of a counter
html:
Compare the region at one visit of the left end with the region at the next, starting from its far (right) end. Most of it is unchanged: only a stretch next to the big block of 1s is rewritten, like the low digits of a counter, where the lowest digits change every time and the higher ones only when a carry reaches them. In the first 3·108 steps (17,520 visits) the rewritten stretch is longer than 20 cells about half the time, longer than 80 cells one time in seven, longer than 320 cells one time in 250.

The short rewrites come from a small repertoire, for example 0101010100 → 010101011 (the block gains two cells; 3,337 times) and 01001110100 → 010011011101 (the block unchanged; 1,378 times). The long ones are different: they replace long stretches with new contents that never recur, so this is not a counter with fixed digits, and its rule is not known yet.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.512). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 32,607 cells (23,545 left of the start, 343 right), with a density of 1s of 0.972.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.
